questions.question: Which is the MOST appropriate intervention in the MCI treatment area?
options: A. Two large-bore IVs for every yellow
B. Routine spinal immobilization of all patients
C. Full secondary survey on every patient
D. Tourniquet and wound packing for hemorrhage
questions.rationale: Hemorrhage control changes survival; the others slow flow without proportional benefit.

questions.question: The nearest hospital is usually overwhelmed early because:
options: A. Self-presenting walking wounded arrive first
D. EMS sends no one there
questions.rationale: Upside-down triage: the least injured self-present to the closest hospital.

questions.question: Which loading plan is MOST efficient?
options: A. Wait until all patients are treated
B. All reds in one ambulance
D. One red + one or two greens per ambulance; greens in bulk by bus with a medic
questions.rationale: Fill seats sensibly and move greens in bulk.

questions.question: A hospital receives 30 casualties in the first hour. Its likely total is about:
questions.rationale: CDC rule of thumb: roughly double the first-hour count.

questions.question: Which patient should be transported FIRST?
options: B. Penetrating torso wound with signs of shock
C. Minor burns to the hand
questions.rationale: Non-compressible torso hemorrhage needs a surgeon now.

questions.question: The main reason to log every transport is to:
options: B. Track each patient's location for families, hospitals, and accountability

questions.question: Which statement about hypothermia in MCIs is TRUE?
options: A. Insulating from the ground is as important as covering
questions.rationale: Ground contact steals heat fast; hypothermia worsens trauma coagulopathy.

questions.question: Hospital capacity during an MCI should be obtained:
options: C. By each crew calling ahead
D. Through the Medical Communications Coordinator / hospital coordination center
questions.rationale: A single channel prevents duplicate calls and gives accurate distribution.
